title: Trabecular architecture remodels to new force patterns after malunited fracture

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Trabecular architecture remodels to new force patterns after malunited fracture

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Trabecular arrangement is produced by the forces acting on the bone, not by heredity: when a fracture heals with the parts displaced so that the stress lines are redistributed, the trabecular system is entirely remodelled within weeks to align with the new forces, even at a distance from the injury.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XVI: On Form and Mechanical Efficiency

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: If a bone be broken and so repaired that its parts lie somewhat out of their former place, so that the pressure-and tension-lines have now a new distribution, before many weeks are over the trabecular system will be found to have been entirely remodelled, so as to fall into line with the new system of forces.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XVI, “On Form and Mechanical Efficiency”; topic “Trabecular architecture and stress lines”. Scope: living vertebrate bone after fracture, malunion or transplantation

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch16-07: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.53

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The prediction is specific, temporal and highly testable in principle. Existing repositories do not provide enough serial microarchitecture plus loading data to resolve it, especially away from the injury.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Use serial CT after malunited fracture to quantify changes in trabecular orientation locally and distally, comparing them with changing finite-element principal stresses and uninjured controls. Complete alignment within weeks is the stated criterion.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Public serial high-resolution scans of malunion are scarce.

The weeks-scale and “entirely remodelled” criteria are demanding.

Clinical CT seldom resolves trabeculae adequately.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.78
operationalizability: 0.9
analysis feasibility: 0.42
data adequacy: 0.22
data existence: 0.35

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The prediction is empirically sharp: a changed load should rewrite the trabecular map within weeks, including away from the break. Clinical descriptions of that remodeling exist as case literature. They do not amount to an open, longitudinal, quantitative dataset on which a small team could confirm or refute the claim.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In malunited fractures, compare trabecular orientation before injury and several weeks later with the principal-stress directions implied by the new alignment, including sites away from the fracture, and contrast those cases with fractures that heal in the original position. Wholesale realignment after displacement, and stability when alignment is unchanged, would support force-driven remodeling over a fixed hereditary pattern.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Published radiographs show selected cases and seldom quantify orientation far from the fracture over a defined number of weeks.

Hospital CT series of malunion are rarely released as research datasets with trabecular resolution.
